proposed:
**The per-variant row is the one commensurable with the vendor rows**, which are also document-level false-negative rates on one adversarially prepared submission. The difference is method, not accounting: our submissions survived an Opus self-screen, making this a stronger attack than a single humanizer pass. The resulting 11.1% point estimate exceeds the 2.31% commercial rate. Clustered on text, however, the per-variant interval is [5.5, 17.6], so the adversarial vendor figures at 2.31–2.86% lie below our estimate but inside its lower tail: the ordering is secure, its margin less so.

The per-target row is italicised because it allows up to eighteen attempts per document, which no published benchmark grants. It is the right number for exposure and the wrong number for a detector comparison. Rice 2026's Australian-Hansard ~8% is deliberately not a row: despite the numeric coincidence, it is a false-*positive* rate on 50 pre-ChatGPT speeches, measured with an LLM judge rather than Pangram (§5). The vendor rows are vendor-reported on undisclosed test data and should be read as such. Independent evaluations (RAID, Dugan et al. 2024; Weber-Wulff et al. 2023) consistently find that detectors fail toward false negatives under obfuscation, the same direction in which our result points.
rationale: This removes an embedded production instruction from the manuscript and eliminates the duplicated Rice explanation without dropping any datum. It applies “one unit, one point” by separating comparability from exclusions and uses the stress position to distinguish the exposure estimate from the benchmark comparison.
